rows.page_name: Residential Soil Lead Directive for CERCLA Sites and RCRA Hazardous Waste Cleanup Facilities | US EPA
rows.brief_description: The EPA’s “Updated Soil Lead Guidance for CERCLA Sites and RCRA Corrective Action Facilities” webpage has been renamed “Residential Soil Lead Directive for CERCLA Sites and RCRA Hazardous Waste Cleanup Facilities.” The page content was overhauled: prior information about 2024 EPA guidance for lead in residential soil under CERCLA was updated to reflect an October 16, 2025 directive by OLEM. The new directive (“Residential Soil Lead Directive for CERCLA Sites and RCRA Hazardous Waste Cleanup Facilities”) supercedes the 2024 guidelines and establishes the following under CERCLA: “regional removal management level of 600 parts per million for lead in residential soil; A regional screening level of 200 parts per million for lead in residential soil; A target children’s blood lead level of 5 micrograms per deciliter to determine preliminary remediation goals; A series of process improvements to accelerate response actions.” This new directive appears *less* protective of human health in residential lead soil cleanups. Whereas the prior 2024 lead directive (see the now overturned, https://semspub.epa.gov/work/HQ/100003435.pdf) took cumulative lead exposures into account, this one does not. Similarly, the “Removal Management Level” (RML) for lead was previously established as 200ppm; this new directive suggests 600ppm.
